reasoning_traces.think:
ENIR extends isotonic regression by constructing an ensemble of near-isotonic models along a regularization path indexed by λ. At λ=0, the model is fully saturated (overfit), whereas larger λ approximates standard isotonic regression. This allows ENIR to relax the strict monotonicity constraint of traditional IsoRegC, which can fail when label mappings are noisy or non-monotonic—such as in linear SVM outputs on circular data. The mPAVA algorithm computes this path efficiently, generating a sequence of models that are then averaged using BIC weights. This dual mechanism ensures both flexibility and generalization. In GSI contexts, this translates into more robust probabilistic forecasts for uncertain outcomes like game scores or player performance. The key insight is that calibration quality improves when we allow deviation from monotonicity, provided we weight models appropriately. The failure mode arises when the base classifier lacks discrimination power; ENIR cannot salvage poor rankers, but it excels where they perform well. Thus, ENIR acts as a plug-and-play enhancement to existing calibration stacks, particularly beneficial in high-noise domains such as sports analytics.
